stem_book: For real t > 0, the equation |x| + |x − 1| = t holds. One or more options may be correct. (a) Infinitely many solutions at t = 1 (b) Two solutions, symmetric about x = 1/2, for every t > 1 (c) No solution for t < 1 (d) Exactly one solution for some t > 1
key: a,b,c Infinitely many solutions at t = 1; Two symmetric solutions for every t > 1; No solution for t < 1
reason: print says only 'two symmetric solutions'; added 'about x = 1/2' so (b) is unambiguously true (they are not symmetric about 0)
work: min of |x|+|x−1| is 1 on [0,1]; t > 1 ⇒ x = (1+t)/2, (1−t)/2 (sum 1, symmetric about 1/2); t < 1 none ⇒ a, b, c
